dto.creator: order-book-tracker
dto.summary: Order book comparison — RVNL Rs 1,05,085 Cr (5.15x FY26 sales), NCC Rs 87,079 Cr (4.18x), KIRLOSENG n/a (no company-wide order book). RVNL leads on multiple; NCC leads on replenishment (FY26 inflow 1.53x sales vs RVNL 0.29x).
dto.question: Compare order books across NSE:RVNL, NSE:NCC and NSE:KIRLOSENG — strongest revenue visibility, plus new orders won since each last concall.

verdict.reasoning: RVNL carries the larger book and the higher book-to-bill (5.15x vs 4.18x) and is the only one with a dated execution calendar (to Dec-2029 on 6 of 7 wins). But its FY26 order inflow of Rs 5,875 Cr covered only 0.29x of sales, so the book is being drawn down, and ~13% of its post-concall additions is GST rather than order value. NCC replenished at 1.53x of sales, grew the book 16% YoY to a record, and reports 74% of it escalation-protected.

caveats: Running totals add gross order wins to a net concall base without subtracting revenue executed since Mar-26, so both read slightly high; the Q1FY27 concall resets the base.
RVNL: 5 of 7 post-concall filings quote value including 18% GST and never state the ex-GST figure; the ex-GST column is derived (/1.18), not filed. Every NCC letter is explicitly excl. GST.
NCC: all three filings are monthly period-aggregate letters, so the stated monthly total is used and its constituent orders are deliberately not added on top.
NCC discloses no execution timeline on any of the three filings, so no execution window can be computed; RVNL states one on 6 of 7.
RVNL 41.04 km and 385 Km buckets are folded to 426.04 Km; MTPA is kept separate as the units share no denominator.
NCC July-2026 monthly order letter had not been filed as of the 2026-07-29 watermark.
Book-to-bill denominators are FY26 consolidated sales from Screener.in, used for all three so the multiples are comparable.
